licenseTiers.label: Standard Baseline
licenseTiers.description: Minimum security controls for all clients regardless of licensing. Leverages free/built-in Microsoft 365 security features (Security Defaults, basic audit, Exchange Online protection defaults, DNS record validation).

licenseTiers.label: P1 / E3 / Business Premium
licenseTiers.description: Additional controls requiring Azure AD Premium P1 (or equivalent via E3/Business Premium). Enables Conditional Access, Intune device management, Microsoft Defender for Business, and basic retention policies.

licenseTiers.label: P2 / Identity Protection
licenseTiers.description: Controls requiring Azure AD Premium P2. Enables Privileged Identity Management (PIM), Identity Protection risk-based policies, and just-in-time admin access.

licenseTiers.label: E5 / Advanced Security
licenseTiers.description: Full E5/EMS E5 security stack. Enables Data Loss Prevention, Insider Risk Management, Microsoft Cloud App Security, Defender for Office 365 P2, Attack Simulation Training, and advanced eDiscovery.

licenseTiers.label: A1 Baseline
licenseTiers.description: Education A1 baseline security controls. Includes Security Defaults, basic EOP anti-malware/anti-phishing, School Data Sync, Education Insights, Teams for Education policies, basic audit, and Secure Score.

licenseTiers.label: A3 Standard
licenseTiers.description: Education A3 controls. Adds Conditional Access, Entra ID Plan 1, Intune for Education, Defender for Endpoint Plan 1, sensitivity labeling, and device management for student/faculty devices.

licenseTiers.label: A5 Advanced
licenseTiers.description: Education A5 full security stack. Adds Entra ID Plan 2, Identity Protection, PIM, Defender for Office 365 Plan 2, Defender for Endpoint Plan 2, DLP, Insider Risk Management, Communication Compliance, and eDiscovery Premium.

items.label: Enforce MFA for all users
items.description: Require multifactor authentication for all user accounts. Use Conditional Access policy targeting 'All users' with MFA grant control, or Security Defaults for unlicensed tenants.
items.guidance: Create CA policy: Assignments > All users > Cloud apps > All cloud apps > Access controls > Grant > Require MFA. Exclude emergency break-glass accounts.
items.verification: Sign-in logs: verify MFA requirement by checking authentication method details. Use 'Require MFA' report in Entra AD.

items.label: Enforce MFA for all admin accounts
items.description: Require MFA for all privileged administrative accounts, including Global Administrators and all role-assignable accounts.
items.guidance: Enable Microsoft's built-in 'Require MFA for admins' Conditional Access policy template, or create a policy targeting all admin roles.
items.verification: Review Entra AD roles assigned to users. Verify MFA challenge appears on admin portal login. Check Conditional Access policy coverage.

items.label: Review MFA registration coverage
items.description: Ensure all users have registered for MFA. Track registration completion and follow up with non-compliant users.
items.guidance: Use Entra AD > Monitoring & health > Authentication methods > Registration. Export users without MFA registered and notify them.
items.verification: Authentication methods report shows >95% registration rate. Run monthly audit of unregistered users.

items.label: Disable legacy authentication
items.description: Block all legacy authentication protocols (Basic Auth, POP, IMAP, SMTP, ActiveSync legacy). These protocols bypass MFA and modern security controls.
items.guidance: Create Conditional Access policy to block legacy auth protocols. Alternatively use Exchange Online Auth Settings to disable per-protocol.
items.verification: Sign-in logs show zero legacy auth attempts. Exchange Online shows all legacy protocols disabled.

items.label: Review password policies
items.description: Review and modernize password policies. Consider enabling password ban lists, removing periodic expiry requirements, and enforcing complexity.
items.guidance: Review Entra ID > Protection > Authentication methods > Password protection. Consider enabling 'Microsoft managed' password ban lists.
items.verification: Password protection settings configured. Custom banned passwords list maintained. Users cannot use common passwords.

items.label: Enable passwordless authentication (optional)
items.description: Deploy passwordless authentication methods: Microsoft Authenticator, FIDO2 security keys, or Windows Hello for Business.
items.guidance: Entra AD > Protection > Authentication methods > Policies. Enable Microsoft Authenticator (passwordless), FIDO2, and/or Windows Hello for Business.
items.verification: Authentication methods report shows passwordless registrations. Test end-to-end passwordless login flow.

items.label: Create baseline Conditional Access policies
items.description: Implement core Conditional Access policies: block legacy auth, require MFA for admins, require MFA for all users, and block unknown/untrusted locations.
items.guidance: Create CA policies in this order: (1) Block legacy auth, (2) Require MFA for admins, (3) Require MFA for all users, (4) Block high-risk sign-ins.
items.verification: All CA policies in 'Enabled' or 'Report-only' state. Sign-in logs show policy enforcement. Report-only policies reviewed within 7 days.

items.label: Require MFA for privileged roles
items.description: Strictly enforce MFA for all Entra ID privileged role assignments. Use Conditional Access policy targeting all privileged roles.
items.guidance: Create CA policy: Assignments > Directory roles > Select all privileged roles > Access controls > Grant > Require MFA. Exclude break-glass accounts.
items.verification: Review CA policy coverage. Audit sign-in logs for privileged role activations without MFA.

items.label: Block risky sign-ins
items.description: Automatically block sign-ins with high risk level. Uses Identity Protection risk detection for real-time blocking.
items.guidance: Identity Protection > User risk policy: Assignments > All users > Conditions > User risk > High > Access > Block access.
items.verification: Identity Protection reports show blocked sign-ins. Risky sign-in report reviewed weekly.

items.label: Block sign-ins from high-risk countries
items.description: Block authentication attempts from geographic locations where the organisation has no business presence.
items.guidance: CA policy: Block access. Condition > Locations > Select locations. Include high-risk or unknown countries. Exclude trusted IPs and break-glass accounts.
items.verification: Sign-in logs show blocked attempts from restricted countries. Review and update location list quarterly.

items.label: Require compliant devices
items.description: Require Intune-managed and compliant devices for access to corporate resources, or at minimum for sensitive data access.
items.guidance: CA policy targeting cloud apps with 'Require device to be marked as compliant' grant. Requires Intune enrollment and compliance policies.
items.verification: Device compliance reports show compliance status. Non-compliant devices blocked from accessing corporate data.

items.label: Configure session timeout policies
items.description: Set session timeout for web apps and browser sessions to limit exposure from unattended access. Use Conditional Access session controls or SharePoint admin settings.
items.guidance: CA policy > Session > Sign-in frequency (every 1-4 hours) and Persistent browser session (never persistent). Apply to all cloud apps except exempted ones.
items.verification: Users prompted for re-authentication after timeout period. Session policies reviewed and enforced.

items.label: Restrict guest access where required
items.description: Implement guest access restrictions based on business requirements. Use Entra ID entitlement management and cross-tenant access settings to control guest access.
items.guidance: Review External Identities > External collaboration settings. Restrict guest invite permissions to specific admin roles. Use entitlement management for governed guest access.
items.verification: Guest user inventory reviewed. Cross-tenant access settings configured. Guest invites limited to authorised admins.

items.label: Review Global Admin accounts
items.description: Audit all Global Administrator assignments. Reduce to absolute minimum (2-4 permanent, rest use PIM). Use break-glass emergency accounts.
items.guidance: Entra AD > Roles & admins > Global Administrator. Review each member. Migrate to PIM for just-in-time. Create 2 cloud-only break-glass accounts with permanent GA role.
items.verification: Global admin count <= 4 permanent + 2 break-glass. All other admins use PIM activation. Break-glass accounts excluded from CA policies.

items.label: Reduce excessive privileged roles
items.description: Audit all privileged role assignments and reduce to minimum necessary. Use Entra ID role-based access control (RBAC) least privilege principle.
items.guidance: Entra AD > Roles & admins > Review each role assignment. Use Privileged Identity Management (if P2 licensed) for eligible assignments. Remove direct assignments where possible.
items.verification: Role assignments audited quarterly. No user has more roles than needed. PIM used for all elevated roles where licensed.

items.label: Separate admin/user accounts
items.description: Ensure administrators have separate accounts for administrative work vs. daily productivity. Admin accounts should be cloud-only where possible.
items.guidance: Create naming convention: admin_@domain or first.last_adm@domain. Admin accounts should not have licenses for email/Office. Remove admin roles from regular user accounts.
items.verification: Review admin role assignments. No user should have both admin roles and a regular user license on same account. Admin accounts separate from productivity accounts.

items.label: Enable Privileged Identity Management (PIM)
items.description: Activate Entra ID PIM for just-in-time privileged role management. Requires Azure AD Premium P2 licensing.
items.guidance: Entra AD > Identity Governance > Privileged Identity Management > Azure AD roles > Settings > Require approval, MFA, and justification for activation. Set maximum activation duration (4-8 hours).
items.verification: PIM dashboard shows eligible assignments. Activation requests logged and approved via configured workflow. No permanent active assignments remain.

items.label: Configure just-in-time admin access
items.description: Configure PIM to enforce just-in-time access. Users activate roles only when needed, with time-bound approvals and audit trail.
items.guidance: In PIM settings: Set 'Maximum activation duration' to 4-8 hours. Require MFA + justification + ticket number on activation. Require approval for high-privilege roles (GA, PA, SA).
items.verification: Review PIM activation logs. No permanent active assignments for high-privilege roles. All activations have justification and approval documented.

items.label: Review inactive/stale accounts
items.description: Identify and remediate inactive or stale user accounts. Disable accounts with no sign-in activity in 90+ days.
items.guidance: Use Entra AD > Monitoring & health > Sign-in logs > Filter by last sign-in > 90 days. Disable inactive accounts. Create automation for recurring review.
items.verification: Monthly report of accounts with no sign-in in 90+ days. Accounts disabled or removed after 120 days of inactivity.

items.label: Configure School Data Sync
items.description: Set up Microsoft School Data Sync (SDS) to automatically import student, teacher, class, and roster data from your SIS into Microsoft 365 Education.
items.guidance: Access SDS via edu.microsoft.com/sds. Connect your SIS (supported: PowerSchool, Infinite Campus, Aeries, etc.) or upload CSV files. Map data fields and sync on schedule. Verify class groups in Teams.
items.verification: SDS sync completed successfully. Classes, students, and teachers appear in Teams for Education. Roster updates sync nightly.

items.label: Enable Education Insights
items.description: Enable Education Insights in Microsoft Teams to provide educators with data-driven insights into student engagement, assignment completion, and digital activity.
items.guidance: Teams Admin Center > Education Insights > Enable. Assign appropriate roles (Insights Administrator, Leader, Educator). Configure data sharing preferences. Review privacy and consent requirements.
items.verification: Education Insights dashboard populated with student engagement data. Educators can view their class insights. Leader dashboard shows institutional trends.

items.label: Automate student account lifecycle
items.description: Implement automated provisioning and deprovisioning of student accounts tied to the academic calendar. Ensure accounts are created before term start and disabled/removed after graduation or withdrawal.
items.guidance: Use SDS for automated provisioning with start/end dates. Configure Entra ID dynamic groups based on student attributes. Set up automated deprovisioning workflows for graduated/withdrawn students. Implement guest student access where appropriate.
items.verification: Student accounts provisioned before term start. Deprovisioned accounts removed within 30 days of graduation. Lifecycle process documented and tested.

items.label: Separate faculty and student Conditional Access policies
items.description: Create distinct Conditional Access policies for faculty/staff vs. students. Students typically require stricter controls (blocked external sharing, restricted hours, no admin access).
items.guidance: Create CA policies targeting 'All Faculty' and 'All Students' dynamic groups. Faculty policies: standard MFA + compliant device. Student policies: block external sharing, restrict to school hours, block legacy auth, require compliant device. Test in report-only mode first.
items.verification: Faculty and students subject to different CA policies. Student policies restrict external access and sharing. Faculty MFA enforced. No policy conflicts between groups.

items.label: Onboard all workstations
items.description: Ensure all workstations are onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (or equivalent EDR solution).
items.guidance: Use Intune or Group Policy to deploy the Defender for Endpoint onboarding package. Verify using MDE portal > Devices > Onboarding status.
items.verification: MDE portal shows >95% workstation coverage. Non-onboarded devices identified and remediated.

items.label: Onboard all servers
items.description: Ensure all servers (on-premises and cloud) are onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
items.guidance: Use MMA or MDE agent deployment for servers. For Azure VMs: Azure Defender auto-provisioning. For on-prem: Group Policy or manual install.
items.verification: MDE portal shows server coverage. Non-covered servers identified in vulnerability management dashboard.

items.label: Validate device health reporting
items.description: Confirm devices are reporting health telemetry correctly to Defender and Intune. Investigate devices with missing or stale data.
items.guidance: MDE > Devices > Filter by 'Inactive' or 'Non-compliant'. Intune > Devices > Device compliance. Remediate devices with stale reporting.
items.verification: Device list in MDE and Intune shows active sensors. No devices with >3 days stale reporting except exempted.

items.label: Enable Tamper Protection
items.description: Enable tamper protection to prevent security settings from being modified by malware or unauthorised processes.
items.guidance: Microsoft 365 Defender > Settings > Endpoints > Advanced features > Tamper protection > On. Also configurable via Intune Endpoint Security > Antivirus policy.
items.verification: Tamper protection status = 'Enabled' across all devices in MDE portal. Weekly report of any devices with protection off.

items.label: Enable Endpoint Detection & Response (EDR)
items.description: Ensure EDR is in active (block) mode, not just audit/alert mode. EDR blocks detected threats automatically.
items.guidance: MDE > Settings > Endpoints > Advanced features > EDR in block mode > On. Verify via Intune endpoint security policies if not applying.
items.verification: All devices show EDR = Active/Block mode. No devices in audit-only mode.

items.label: Enable automated investigation and remediation
items.description: Enable automated investigation and response for alerts to reduce manual SOC workload and improve response times.
items.guidance: M365 Defender > Settings > Endpoints > Automated investigation > Enabled. Set automation level to 'Full - remediate threats automatically'.
items.verification: Automated investigation reports show actions taken. Review monthly for effectiveness and false positives.

items.label: Configure antivirus policies
items.description: Deploy Microsoft Defender Antivirus policies centrally via Intune or GPO. Ensure real-time protection, cloud-delivered protection, and regular scans are configured.
items.guidance: Intune > Endpoint Security > Antivirus > Create policy (Windows 10/11 template). Enable cloud protection, real-time monitoring, scheduled scans (quick scan daily).
items.verification: Antivirus policy applied to all devices. Defender AV status shows Active. Cloud protection enabled.

items.label: Confirm Defender AV is in active mode
items.description: Ensure Microsoft Defender Antivirus is running in active mode, not passive mode or disabled. Passive mode means another AV is primary.
items.guidance: Check via Intune > Devices > Antivirus status. Defender should show 'Active' and 'Real-time protection enabled'. If passive, uninstall third-party AV or configure co-existence properly.
items.verification: All Windows devices show Defender AV = Active mode. No devices showing Passive or EDR-blocked mode.

items.label: Configure ASR rules
items.description: Deploy Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules to block common malware behaviours. Use audit mode initially, then block mode.
items.guidance: Intune > Endpoint Security > Attack Surface Reduction > ASR rules. Enable key rules: Block Office child process, Block executable from email, Block credential stealing, Block PSExec/WMI lateral movement.
items.verification: ASR rules enabled in block mode. Review ASR event log (Event ID 1121) for blocked activities. Address false positives via exclusions.

items.label: Block Office macro abuse
items.description: Block macros from running in Office files from the internet. Use GPO or Intune to enforce macro security settings.
items.guidance: Set 'Block macros from running in Office files from the Internet' via GPO or Intune OMA-URI. ASR rule 'Block Office communication application from creating child processes' also applies.
items.verification: Macro abuse attempts blocked. Users cannot enable macros from internet-sourced documents without approval process.

items.label: Restrict executable content from email/web
items.description: Block dangerous executable file types from being downloaded via email or web. Use Exchange Online and Defender for Office 365 policies.
items.guidance: Exchange Online > Mail flow > Malware filter > Common attachments filter. Enable 'Filter common attachments' list. Also leverage Safe Attachments.
items.verification: Executable file types blocked from email. Test by sending .exe, .scr, .ps1 attachments.

items.label: Configure controlled folder access
items.description: Enable Controlled Folder Access (CFA) to protect sensitive folders from ransomware encryption. Monitor and manage protected folders.
items.guidance: Intune > Endpoint Security > Attack Surface Reduction > Controlled folder access. Enable in Block mode. Configure protected folders (Documents, Desktop, Pictures) and trusted apps.
items.verification: CFA enabled on all devices. Review CFA events for false positives. Trusted apps list maintained and current.

items.label: Configure ransomware protection
items.description: Deploy comprehensive ransomware protection: Controlled Folder Access, ASR rules, EDR in block mode, and MDO Safe Attachments.
items.guidance: Enable all Defender layers: ASR rules, CFA, EDR block mode, Tamper Protection, and MDO Safe Attachments. Test ransomware simulation scenarios.
items.verification: All ransomware protection layers active. Monthly review of protection coverage. Test isolation capability.

items.label: Configure Intune compliance policies
items.description: Define device compliance requirements: OS minimum version, device health attestation, password/PIN requirements, encryption status, and threat level.
items.guidance: Intune > Devices > Compliance policies > Create policy. Set requirements: Device health (BitLocker, Secure Boot, TPM), OS minimum version, password length/complexity. Assign to all devices.
items.verification: Compliance policy dashboard shows >90% compliant. Non-compliant devices trigger CA policy to block access.

items.label: Configure device encryption policies
items.description: Enforce device encryption on all endpoints. Use BitLocker for Windows, FileVault for macOS via Intune.
items.guidance: Intune > Endpoint Security > Disk encryption > Create policy for Windows (BitLocker) and macOS (FileVault). Configure recovery key escrow to Entra ID.
items.verification: Device encryption status active on all devices. BitLocker recovery keys backed up to Entra ID. No unencrypted devices.

items.label: Enable BitLocker management
items.description: Centrally manage BitLocker via Intune. Escrow recovery keys to Entra ID. Configure encryption method (XTS-AES 256-bit) and silent encryption.
items.guidance: Intune > Endpoint Security > Disk encryption > Windows. Enable: 'Require device encryption', 'Enable FIPS-compliant recovery', 'Store recovery key in Entra ID'. Set XTS-AES 256-bit.
items.verification: Recovery keys visible in Entra ID > Devices > BitLocker keys. Encryption status = Fully encrypted on all devices.

items.label: Configure USB/device control
items.description: Implement USB device control to restrict removable storage. Allow only approved USB devices and block unauthorised peripherals.
items.guidance: Intune > Endpoint Security > Attack Surface Reduction > Removable storage. Set 'Removable storage' to Block. Create exclusion list for authorised devices.
items.verification: Unauthorised USB devices blocked from writing data. Authorised devices function correctly. Exceptions documented and approved.

items.label: Configure web content filtering
items.description: Enable web content filtering via Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps or Defender for Endpoint web protection to block malicious/high-risk sites.
items.guidance: MDE > Settings > Endpoints > Web protection > Enable. Configure custom indicator policies to block/allow categories. Use Defender for Cloud Apps for deeper filtering.
items.verification: Web threat detections visible in MDE. Blocked URL reports generated and reviewed weekly.

items.label: Test device isolation functionality
items.description: Verify that device isolation (network quarantine) works correctly. Isolate a test device and confirm it can communicate with Defender but not the network.
items.guidance: MDE > Device inventory > Select device > Actions > Isolate device. Verify: Device can still phone home to Defender, but cannot access other network resources.
items.verification: Test isolation successful. De-isolation tested and works. Process documented for SOC/engineering teams.

items.label: Enable Threat & Vulnerability Management
items.description: Enable Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management (MDVM) for continuous vulnerability assessment and prioritisation.
items.guidance: MDE > Settings > Endpoints > General > Vulnerability management > On. TVM automatically enabled with MDE onboarding.
items.verification: Vulnerability management dashboard populated with data. Top vulnerabilities identified and remediation tickets created.

items.label: Review high-risk vulnerabilities
items.description: Weekly review of critical and high severity vulnerabilities identified by TVM. Prioritise and assign remediation tasks.
items.guidance: MDE > Vulnerability management > Weaknesses > Filter by severity: Critical, High. Export list, assign owners, and track remediation progress in ticket system.
items.verification: Weekly TVM review completed. Critical vulnerabilities remediated within SLA (7 days). High vulnerabilities within 30 days.

items.label: Establish remediation process
items.description: Create formal vulnerability remediation process: Identification > Triage > Assignment > Remediation > Verification. Define SLAs per severity level.
items.guidance: Document response SLAs: Critical=7 days, High=30 days, Medium=90 days. Define escalation path for missed SLAs. Integrate with existing ticketing system.
items.verification: Remediation process documented and visible to team. SLAs tracked and reported monthly.

items.label: Review exposed devices monthly
items.description: Monthly review of devices with highest vulnerability exposure scores. Prioritise remediation for most exposed devices.
items.guidance: MDE > Vulnerability management > Most exposed devices. Review top 10 most exposed devices monthly. Create remediation plan for each.
items.verification: Monthly report generated. Exposure scores trending downward. Top 10 exposed devices receive remediation within 30 days.

items.label: Configure Intune for Education
items.description: Set up Intune for Education to manage student and faculty devices. Enroll Windows, iOS, and Android devices with education-specific configuration profiles.
items.guidance: Access Intune for Education at edu.microsoft.com/intune. Configure device enrollment: Auto-pilot for Windows, Apple School Manager for iOS, Android for Education. Create configuration profiles for student devices (kiosk mode, app restrictions, content filtering).
items.verification: Devices enrolling successfully through education enrollment flows. Student devices in kiosk or restricted mode. Faculty devices have standard management. Compliance policies applied.

items.label: Configure student device policies
items.description: Define device management policies specifically for student-used devices including shared devices, loaner programs, and BYOD. Restrict app installation, enforce web filtering, and block administrative access.
items.guidance: Intune > Devices > Configuration profiles > Create student profile: Restrict app store to Education apps only, Enable kiosk mode for shared devices, Block admin rights, Enforce web content filtering via Defender, Set screen time limits. Apply to student device groups.
items.verification: Student devices restricted to approved apps only. Web filtering active. No students have admin rights on managed devices. Shared devices reset properly between sessions.

items.label: Enable Safe Links
items.description: Enable Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Safe Links to protect users from malicious URLs in email messages and Office documents.
items.guidance: Microsoft 365 Defender > Email & collaboration > Policies & rules > Threat policies > Safe Links. Create policy for all recipients: Enable URL scanning, track clicks, block URLs in email and Teams.
items.verification: Safe Links policy applied to all users. URL click tracking shows blocked malicious URLs. Review Safe Links reports weekly.

items.label: Enable Safe Attachments
items.description: Enable Safe Attachments to detect and block malicious attachments in email. Use dynamic delivery for safe user experience.
items.guidance: Microsoft 365 Defender > Threat policies > Safe Attachments > Create policy. Set: 'Safe Attachments unknown malware response' = Block. Enable 'Dynamic delivery' to allow safe preview.
items.verification: Safe Attachments policy applied to all recipients. Attachments detonated in sandbox. Malicious attachments blocked and reported.

items.label: Configure anti-phishing policies
items.description: Configure Defender for Office 365 anti-phishing protection including impersonation protection, spoof intelligence, and mailbox intelligence.
items.guidance: M365 Defender > Threat policies > Anti-phishing > Default policy (or create new). Enable: Impersonation protection (domain + user), Mailbox intelligence, Spoof intelligence, Advanced phishing thresholds.
items.verification: Anti-phishing policy protecting all users. Impersonation attempts blocked/quarantined. Spoofed domains detected.

items.label: Configure impersonation protection
items.description: Set up impersonation protection for key executives and domains. Add CEO, CFO, and other VIPs as protected users.
items.guidance: M365 Defender > Threat policies > Anti-phishing > Impersonation. Add protected users (C-suite, finance team). Add protected domains (your domains and partner domains).
items.verification: Top executives protected. Impersonation attempts detected and quarantined. Monthly review of impersonation detections.

items.label: Configure anti-spam policies
items.description: Tune anti-spam connection and content filters. Set bulk email threshold to protect users while minimising false positives.
items.guidance: Exchange Admin Center > mail flow > Spam filter. Set: Spam action = Move to Junk (or Quarantine for stricter), Bulk threshold = 4 or lower. Enable bulk complaint level (BCL) filtering.
items.verification: Users report reduced spam. Quarantine policy reviewed weekly. False positives minimised.

items.label: Enable user-reported phishing
items.description: Enable the Microsoft Report Message add-in and integrate with M365 Defender for user-reported phishing analysis.
items.guidance: M365 Defender > Email & collaboration > Policies > User reported messages. Enable 'Use Microsoft Outlook Report Message add-in'. Configure where messages are sent (Microsoft for analysis).
items.verification: Users can report phishing via Outlook add-in. Reported messages visible in M365 Defender. Automated analysis triggered on user reports.

items.label: Validate SPF records
items.description: Ensure SPF (Sender Policy Framework) DNS record is correctly configured for all custom domains to prevent email spoofing.
items.guidance: Check SPF record: v=spf1 include:spf.protection.outlook.com -all. Use MXToolbox or similar for validation. Include all legitimate email sources.
items.verification: SPF record passes DNS validation. No legitimate emails failing SPF check. SPF record reviewed quarterly.

items.label: Enable DKIM
items.description: Configure DKIM signing for all custom domains to cryptographically sign outgoing emails and prevent tampering.
items.guidance: Exchange Admin Center > Protection > dkim > Select domain > Enable. Or use PowerShell: New-DkimSigningConfig -DomainName domain.com -Enabled $true. Publish CNAME records as provided.
items.verification: DKIM signing active on all domains. Email headers show dkim=pass. DKIM rotation enabled (second key pair).

items.label: Configure DMARC
items.description: Configure DMARC policy to instruct receiving mail servers how to handle unauthenticated email from your domain. Start with p=none, move to p=quarantine, then p=reject.
items.guidance: Create DMARC TXT record: _dmarc.domain.com. Start with p=none with rua reports. Monitor for 2+ weeks. Move to p=quarantine, then p=reject once confident. Set pct=100.
items.verification: DMARC record published. Aggregate reports received and reviewed. DMARC policy at p=reject for all domains.

items.label: Review external forwarding rules
items.description: Audit and restrict external email forwarding rules. Remote-domain auto-forwarding should be blocked by default unless explicitly approved.
items.guidance: Exchange Admin Center > Mail flow > Auto-forwarding. Set: 'Automatic forwarding' = 'Blocked - Control by remote domains'. Use Mail Flow rule to block external auto-forwarding unless approved.
items.verification: External forwarding rules audited. Unapproved forwarding rules disabled. New forwarding rules require approval.

items.label: Audit shared mailbox permissions
items.description: Review and audit shared mailbox permissions. Remove excessive access and ensure only required users have Send-As or Full Access permissions.
items.guidance: Exchange Admin Center > Recipients > Shared mailboxes. Review permissions for each. Use PowerShell: Get-MailboxPermission -Identity shared@domain.com. Audit quarterly.
items.verification: Shared mailbox permissions reviewed. No users have unnecessary access. Send-As permissions limited to approved staff.

items.label: Review mail transport rules
items.description: Review all Exchange mail flow rules (transport rules) for security relevance. Remove obsolete rules and ensure encryption/security rules are in place.
items.guidance: Exchange Admin Center > Mail flow > Rules. Review each rule for purpose and effectiveness. Add rules for: encrypt sensitive content, block external auto-forwarding, add disclaimers.
items.verification: Transport rules documented and reviewed. No obsolete rules remain. Rules for data protection and compliance are active.

items.label: Review external sharing settings
items.description: Restrict SharePoint/OneDrive external sharing to authenticated users only. Disable 'Anyone' (anonymous) sharing links by default.
items.guidance: SharePoint Admin Center > Policies > Sharing. Set: 'External sharing' to 'New and existing guests'. Disable 'Anyone' links. Enable domain allow/block lists.
items.verification: SharePoint external sharing restricted. No anonymous/Anyone links active. External sharing report reviewed quarterly.

items.label: Restrict anonymous sharing
items.description: Ensure anonymous/Anyone sharing links are disabled across SharePoint and OneDrive. Only specific people sharing should be allowed.
items.guidance: SharePoint Admin > Policies > Sharing > 'Anyone' links > Off. Set 'Default link type' to 'Specific people' for both SharePoint and OneDrive.
items.verification: No Anyone links created in last 90 days. Default link type = Specific people. Users must explicitly request external sharing.

items.label: Review guest user permissions
items.description: Review and restrict guest user permissions across Microsoft 365. Ensure guests have minimal access aligned with business requirements.
items.guidance: Entra AD > External Identities > External collaboration settings. Set: Guest invite restricted to admins. Guest access limited to properties and memberships of their own objects.
items.verification: Guest access levels aligned with business needs. Guest accounts reviewed quarterly. Excessive guest permissions removed.

items.label: Configure file-sharing policies
items.description: Set unified file-sharing policies across SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams. Control external sharing, download restrictions, and session controls.
items.guidance: Configure: SharePoint admin > Policies > Sharing (external, link types). CA policy > Session > Use app-enforced restrictions for SharePoint/OneDrive. Sensitivity labels for file protection.
items.verification: File-sharing policies applied across all workloads. External sharing restricted. Users cannot share beyond configured policies.

items.label: Enable sensitivity labels for collaboration
items.description: Enable sensitivity labels for SharePoint and Teams sites to classify and control access to collaborative content.
items.guidance: Microsoft Purview > Information protection > Labels. Create labels: Internal, Confidential, Highly Confidential. Assign container protection settings (privacy, external sharing). Publish to all users.
items.verification: Sensitivity labels published and visible in SharePoint/Teams. Labels applied to sites. External sharing controlled via labels.

items.label: Configure Teams for Education policies
items.description: Set up Microsoft Teams policies specifically for education: control student chat, meeting creation, private channels, and content sharing based on role.
items.guidance: Teams Admin Center > Teams policies > Create policy for Students: Disable private chat (or supervise), block meeting creation, limit channel creation to educators. Create separate policy for Faculty: standard collaboration features. Apply policies via group policy assignment.
items.verification: Students have restricted Teams capabilities. Faculty have full collaboration features. Chat supervision active for younger students. Policies applied consistently.

items.label: Enable student communication safety
items.description: Configure communication safety features for students including supervised chat, content filtering, and blocking inappropriate content in Teams and Exchange.
items.guidance: Teams Admin Center > Messaging policies > Supervised chat for student groups. Enable Exchange Online Content Filtering for student mailboxes. Configure allowed/blocked domains for student communication. Use communication compliance (A5) for advanced monitoring.
items.verification: Student chat supervised or restricted. Inappropriate content filtered in email and Teams. Communication safety settings tested with sample scenarios.

items.label: Enable audit logging
items.description: Enable unified audit logging in Microsoft 365 to capture user and admin activity across all workloads for security investigations and compliance.
items.guidance: Microsoft Purview > Audit > Solutions > Audit > Start recording user and admin activity (ON by default for E5, may need enabling for lower SKUs). Enable at least 180-day retention.
items.verification: Audit log search returning results. Audit log retention set to minimum 180 days (or longer for E5 with retention policies).

items.label: Configure retention policies
items.description: Define and apply retention policies for email, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, and Exchange to meet legal and compliance obligations.
items.guidance: Microsoft Purview > Data Lifecycle Management > Microsoft 365 > Retention policies. Create policies by workload: Email (7 years), Documents (7 years), Teams messages (1 year). Apply to all locations.
items.verification: Retention policies applied. Audit log shows retention actions. Policy effectiveness reviewed semi-annually.

items.label: Configure Data Loss Prevention (DLP)
items.description: Implement DLP policies to detect and prevent inadvertent sharing of sensitive information via email, SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams.
items.guidance: Microsoft Purview > Data Loss Prevention > Microsoft 365 > Create policy. Start with templates: Financial, Medical, Privacy. Test in audit mode first, then enforce. Monitor DLP alerts daily.
items.verification: DLP policies active and enforcing. DLP alerts reviewed daily. False positives tuned. Sensitive data detections logged and investigated.

items.label: Configure sensitivity labels
items.description: Create and publish sensitivity labels to classify and protect data based on sensitivity. Apply encryption and visual markings.
items.guidance: Microsoft Purview > Information protection > Labels. Create label hierarchy: Internal, Confidential, Highly Confidential. Configure encryption for Confidential+ labels. Publish via label policy to all users.
items.verification: Sensitivity labels visible in Office apps. Users applying labels. Encryption enforced on labeled documents. Labels used in DLP policies.

items.label: Configure auto-labeling policies
items.description: Create auto-labeling policies to automatically apply sensitivity labels to documents containing sensitive information types.
items.guidance: Microsoft Purview > Information protection > Auto-labeling > Create policy. Run in simulation mode first. Identify sensitive data patterns (credit cards, passport numbers, etc.). Auto-apply labels after validation.
items.verification: Auto-labeling policies in simulation/review mode. Sensitive documents automatically labeled. Accuracy validated before enforcement.

items.label: Review data classification requirements
items.description: Identify and document regulatory and business data classification requirements. Map to sensitivity labels and DLP policies.
items.guidance: Document: What data does your organisation hold? What regulations apply (POPIA, GDPR, PCI-DSS, HIPAA)? Map each data type to a sensitivity label. Define handling requirements.
items.verification: Data classification requirements documented. Label taxonomy aligned with regulatory requirements. Reviewed annually.

items.label: Protect financial information
items.description: Configure data protection controls specifically for financial information (PCI-DSS compliance). DLP policy to detect and protect financial data.
items.guidance: Microsoft Purview > DLP > Financial data template. Include credit card numbers, SWIFT codes, bank account numbers. Use audit mode initially, then enforce. Restrict sharing of financial documents.
items.verification: Financial information protected by DLP. PCI-DSS scope reduced. Credit card data not stored in email or documents without protection.

items.label: Protect identity/passport information
items.description: Configure DLP to detect and protect personally identifiable information (PII) such as passport numbers, ID numbers, and other identity data.
items.guidance: Microsoft Purview > DLP > Privacy regulations template. Include: Passport numbers, National ID numbers, Driver's license numbers. Apply stricter controls for cross-border sharing.
items.verification: PII detected and protected. DLP alerts for PII reviewed. Sharing of PII restricted to authorised personnel only.

items.label: Restrict sensitive external sharing
items.description: Block external sharing of documents containing sensitive information types. Use DLP and sensitivity labels to enforce restrictions.
items.guidance: DLP rule: Detect sensitive info types AND external sharing = Block. Also configure sensitivity labels to block external sharing for Confidential and Highly Confidential labels.
items.verification: Sensitive documents cannot be shared externally. DLP blocks attempted external sharing. Labels prevent users from over-sharing.

items.label: Configure insider risk policies
items.description: Set up insider risk management policies to detect potentially malicious insider activities such as data exfiltration, IP theft, and policy violations.
items.guidance: Microsoft Purview > Insider Risk Management > Policies. Create policies for: Data theft by departing users, Data leaks by priority users, Unauthorised data exfiltration. Start in audit mode.
items.verification: Insider risk policies active. Alerts generated for suspicious activities. Policies reviewed and tuned monthly.

items.label: Configure eDiscovery readiness
items.description: Set up eDiscovery capabilities for legal hold, content search, and case management. Ensure audit logs and retention policies support eDiscovery requirements.
items.guidance: Microsoft Purview > eDiscovery > Standard or Premium. Create eDiscovery cases. Place custodians on legal hold. Configure communication workflows. Train legal/compliance team on tool use.
items.verification: eDiscovery case management ready. Legal hold policies tested. Content searches return expected results. Team trained on eDiscovery.

items.label: Configure student data privacy controls
items.description: Implement data privacy controls to protect student PII in compliance with FERPA, POPIA, GDPR, or regional education privacy regulations. Use DLP and sensitivity labels to safeguard student records.
items.guidance: Microsoft Purview > Data Loss Prevention > Create education-specific DLP policy: Detect student PII (ID numbers, grades, medical info). Block external sharing of student records. Apply 'Highly Confidential' sensitivity label to student record repositories. Enable audit logging for all access to student data.
items.verification: Student PII detected and protected. DLP policies blocking unauthorized sharing. Sensitivity labels applied to student record sites. Compliance with applicable education privacy regulations documented.

items.label: Configure incident notifications
items.description: Set up email/SMS notifications for security incidents to ensure SOC team is alerted promptly on high-severity alerts.
items.guidance: Microsoft 365 Defender > Settings > Email notifications. Add SOC team emails for: Critical severity alerts, Admin action required, New incidents assigned to your team.
items.verification: Notifications delivered consistently. SOC team acknowledges alerts within SLA. Test notification delivery monthly.

items.label: Configure SOC/security alert routing
items.description: Configure automated routing of security alerts to SOC team or SIEM. Use M365 Defender APIs, Logic Apps, or third-party integrations.
items.guidance: M365 Defender > Settings > APIs. Enable: SIEM integration, Microsoft Graph API, or custom Logic App connector. Route high-severity alerts to SOC ticket system and Teams channel.
items.verification: Alerts reaching SOC team within 5 minutes of detection. Routing tested monthly. SOC acknowledges receipt.

items.label: Review incident severity settings
items.description: Review and tune incident severity classification to reduce noise and ensure high-severity incidents get appropriate attention.
items.guidance: M365 Defender > Incidents > Filter by severity. Review severity distribution. Tune detection rules to reduce medium/low noise if overwhelming. Ensure critical incidents trigger immediate response.
items.verification: Incident severity distribution balanced. No critical incidents missed due to noise. Severity tuning reviewed monthly.

items.label: Enable unified security monitoring
items.description: Enable Microsoft 365 Defender unified portal as the single pane of glass for all security monitoring across email, identity, endpoints, and cloud apps.
items.guidance: Access security.microsoft.com. Ensure all workloads (MDO, MDE, MDI, MCAS) are integrated. Configure cross-workload correlation for incident detection.
items.verification: Unified portal shows incidents across all workloads. Cross-workload correlations detected. SOC uses unified portal as primary monitoring tool.

items.label: Review alert suppression rules
items.description: Create alert suppression rules to reduce noise from known benign activities. Regularly review and tune suppression rules to avoid missing genuine threats.
items.guidance: M365 Defender > Settings > Alert suppression. Create rules for known false positives. Set expiration dates on suppression rules to force periodic review.
items.verification: Alert suppression rules documented. No critical alerts suppressed accidentally. Rules reviewed quarterly.

items.label: Review current Secure Score
items.description: Establish baseline Secure Score and track improvements. Review Microsoft Secure Score dashboard for recommended improvement actions.
items.guidance: Access https://security.microsoft.com/securescore. Review current score. Note top 10 improvement actions with highest point impact. Assign owners.
items.verification: Secure Score documented monthly. Score improving over time. Top improvement actions actioned.

items.label: Identify improvement actions
items.description: From Secure Score, identify and prioritise improvement actions based on impact and effort. Create remediation project plan.
items.guidance: Export Secure Score improvement actions to CSV. Categorise by: Quick wins (low effort, high impact), Strategic (high effort, high impact), Deferred (low impact).
items.verification: Improvement action plan documented. Monthly progress tracked. Score improving month over month.

items.label: Establish Secure Score targets
items.description: Set target Secure Score for each client based on their licensing. E5 targets should be higher than Standard targets.
items.guidance: Define targets: Standard ≥ 70%, P1/E3 ≥ 75%, P2 ≥ 80%, E5 ≥ 85%. Track progress against targets monthly. Escalate if score stagnates.
items.verification: Secure Score targets documented. Monthly tracking against targets. Action plans in place for clients below target.

items.label: Track score improvement monthly
items.description: Generate monthly Secure Score report showing improvement over time. Share with client stakeholders and engineering teams.
items.guidance: Download Secure Score history monthly. Create trend chart in your reporting tool. Include: Current score, Target, MoM change, Top 3 improvements made, Top 3 outstanding actions.
items.verification: Monthly score report generated and delivered. Score trending upward. Client engaged in improvement process.

items.label: Create executive security dashboard
items.description: Build an executive-level security dashboard showing key metrics: Secure Score, incidents, MFA coverage, compliance status, and remediation progress.
items.guidance: Identify 5-8 key metrics. Use M365 Defender APIs to pull data. Create dashboard in Power BI or similar tool. Schedule weekly/ monthly distribution.
items.verification: Executive dashboard operational. Stakeholders review monthly. Metrics show improvement over time.

items.label: Create monthly security reporting
items.description: Generate comprehensive monthly security report covering: incidents, threats blocked, vulnerabilities, Secure Score, baseline compliance, and outstanding actions.
items.guidance: Template report sections: Executive Summary, Incident Activity, Threat Landscape, Vulnerability Status, Secure Score Progress, Baseline Compliance, Action Items. Distribute to client/management.
items.verification: Monthly reports delivered consistently. Clients engage with report content. Action items tracked to closure.

items.label: Monitor high-risk users
items.description: Proactively monitor users flagged as high-risk by Identity Protection. Investigate and remediate compromised accounts promptly.
items.guidance: Entra AD > Protection > Identity Protection > Risky users. Review daily. Investigate high-risk users: confirm compromise, reset passwords, revoke sessions, investigate root cause.
items.verification: Risky user reports reviewed daily. High-risk users remediated within 24 hours. User risk scores trending down.

items.label: Monitor risky devices
items.description: Monitor and investigate devices flagged as compromised or risky. Use MDE to isolate and remediate compromised devices.
items.guidance: MDE > Device inventory > Risk level filter. Review high-risk devices. Investigate alerts generated. Isolate device if compromise confirmed. Remediate and restore.
items.verification: Risky device inventory reviewed daily. High-risk devices investigated within 4 hours. Compromised devices isolated promptly.

items.label: Monitor phishing trends
items.description: Track phishing attack trends across the tenant. Analyse user-reported phishing, Safe Links detections, and impersonation attempts to identify patterns.
items.guidance: M365 Defender > Threat explorer > Phishing. Review weekly: Top targeted users, New impersonation domains, User click rates on malicious links, Safe Links detections.
items.verification: Phishing trend reports generated weekly. High-risk users identified and trained. Click-through rates decreasing over time.

items.label: Review Conditional Access insights
items.description: Use Conditional Access insights and reporting to monitor policy effectiveness. Review sign-in failures caused by CA policies and tune accordingly.
items.guidance: Entra AD > Monitoring & health > Sign-in logs > Filter by Conditional Access status. Review: What-If tool for new policies, CA insights workbook, Policy impact on sign-in success rate.
items.verification: CA insights report reviewed weekly. Policy tuning done based on user impact. New policies tested in Report-only mode before enforcement.

items.label: Configure education-specific threat monitoring
items.description: Set up monitoring for threats targeting education institutions including phishing campaigns targeting students, ransomware, and inappropriate content sharing.
items.guidance: M365 Defender > Incidents > Create alert rules for education-specific scenarios: mass student account compromise, unusual after-hours access by student accounts, bulk file downloads by students. Enable Defender for Office 365 for student mailboxes. Set up alert notifications for IT/security staff.
items.verification: Education-specific threat monitoring active. Alerts generated for student account anomalies. IT staff receives notifications. Monthly threat review for education-specific patterns.

items.label: Enable user risk policies
items.description: Configure Identity Protection user risk policy to automatically block or remediate users with high-risk detections.
items.guidance: Entra AD > Identity Protection > User risk policy. Set: User risk = High, Action = Block access or Require password change. Apply to All users.
items.verification: User risk policy enabled. High-risk users automatically remediated. Risky user report monitored daily.

items.label: Enable sign-in risk policies
items.description: Configure Identity Protection sign-in risk policy to block high-risk sign-in attempts in real-time.
items.guidance: Entra AD > Identity Protection > Sign-in risk policy. Set: Sign-in risk = High, Action = Block access. Apply to All users. Exclude break-glass accounts.
items.verification: Sign-in risk policy enabled. High-risk sign-ins blocked. Sign-in risk reports reviewed weekly.

items.label: Configure impossible travel detection
items.description: Configure risk detection for sign-ins from geographically impossible locations within short timeframes, indicating token replay or credential theft.
items.guidance: Built into Identity Protection. Enable: Sign-in risk detection includes 'Impossible travel'. No separate configuration needed - ensure Identity Protection is enabled with P2 licenses.
items.verification: Impossible travel detections reviewed in ID Protection reports. Alerts generated when detected. High-confidence detections result in blocked sign-ins.

items.label: Configure anonymous IP alerts
items.description: Monitor and alert on sign-ins originating from anonymous IP addresses (TOR networks, VPNs, proxies) for non-approved scenarios.
items.guidance: Built into Identity Protection detection. Use Conditional Access policy to block or require additional verification for sign-ins from anonymous IPs. CA > Sign-in risk > Anonymous IP.
items.verification: Anonymous IP sign-ins detected and alerted. Blocked if from outside approved remote access channels.

items.label: Review risky sign-in reports
items.description: Weekly review of risky sign-in reports from Identity Protection. Investigate and remediate confirmed compromises.
items.guidance: Entra AD > Protection > Identity Protection > Risky sign-ins. Review weekly patterns: Atypical travel, Anonymous IP, Malware-linked IP, Leaked credentials. Remediate confirmed compromise: force password reset, revoke tokens.
items.verification: Weekly risky sign-in report completed. Confirmed compromises remediated within 24 hours. Report documented and filed.

items.label: Enable Cloud App Security
items.description: Enable Microsoft Cloud App Security (MCAS) for cloud app discovery, risk assessment, session controls, and advanced anomaly detection.
items.guidance: Microsoft 365 Defender > Cloud Apps > Connect apps. Connect Microsoft 365, Azure, and third-party apps. Enable Cloud Discovery for shadow IT identification. Deploy Defender for Cloud Apps log collector for on-prem traffic.
items.verification: MCAS integration active. Connected apps visible. Cloud Discovery reporting data. Session controls working for sanctioned apps.

items.label: Review shadow IT applications
items.description: Continuously discover and assess shadow IT applications used by users. Sanction or block applications based on risk assessment.
items.guidance: MCAS > Cloud Discovery > Dashboard. Review discovered apps sorted by users, traffic, or risk score. Sanction approved apps. Block high-risk/unsanctioned apps via MCAS access policies.
items.verification: Shadow IT report reviewed weekly. High-risk apps blocked. Sanctioned apps monitored for compliance. User count on unsanctioned apps trending down.

items.label: Configure risky behavior alerts
items.description: Set up policy templates in Cloud App Security for risky user behavior: impossible travel, mass download, unusual file sharing, and malware detection.
items.guidance: MCAS > Policies > Policy templates. Enable: Impossible travel, Activity from anonymous IP, Mass download by a single user, Unusual file sharing activity, Malware detection. Configure alert thresholds.
items.verification: Risky behavior policies active. Alerts generated on suspicious activity. Alerts reviewed and investigated within 24 hours.

items.label: Monitor mass download activity
items.description: Configure MCAS to detect and alert on mass download activity that could indicate data exfiltration by insiders or compromised accounts.
items.guidance: MCAS > Policies > Create policy: Activity policy > Single activity > Download > Multiple failed attempts. Set threshold: >10 downloads per hour or >50 downloads per day. Alert SOC.
items.verification: Mass download alerts reviewed. False positives tuned. Data exfiltration attempts detected and investigated.

items.label: Configure unmanaged device controls
items.description: Use MCAS session controls to restrict access from unmanaged devices. Enforce read-only access, block downloads, and require AUP acceptance.
items.guidance: MCAS > Policies > Session policy > Device tags. Create policy: If device = 'unmanaged', then restrict session (block download, set read-only). Assign to sensitive cloud apps (SharePoint, OneDrive, Power BI).
items.verification: Session controls active for unmanaged devices. Downloads blocked for unmanaged sessions. Read-only mode enforced. User experience acceptable.

items.label: Configure Attack Simulation Training
items.description: Set up Microsoft's Attack Simulation Training to create and launch phishing simulation campaigns for security awareness training.
items.guidance: Microsoft 365 Defender > Email & collaboration > Attack simulation training > Simulations > Launch simulation. Choose payloads from built-in library (credential harvest, malware, link phishing). Configure landing page training.
items.verification: Attack simulation training enabled. At least one simulation run in last 90 days. User click rates tracked. Training completion rates > 90%.

items.label: Launch phishing simulations
items.description: Run regular phishing simulations to test user awareness and identify users who require additional security training.
items.guidance: M365 Defender > Attack simulation > Create simulation. Target: All users or high-risk users. Use diverse payloads (credential phishing, attachment, link). Schedule quarterly. Assign training to users who click.
items.verification: Phishing simulations run quarterly. Click-through rate improving quarter over quarter. High-risk users assigned targeted training.

items.label: Review user risk scores
items.description: Monthly review of Identity Protection user risk scores. Investigate persistent high-risk users and address root causes.
items.guidance: Entra AD > Identity Protection > Risky users > Sort by Risk level. Investigate persistent medium/high-risk users. Common causes: leaked credentials, suspicious sign-ins, malware. Remediate: password reset, revoke sessions, educate user.
items.verification: Monthly risk score review completed. High-risk users remediated. No user has persistent high risk for >30 days.

items.label: Schedule awareness campaigns
items.description: Plan and execute regular security awareness campaigns. Use Attack Simulation Training to deliver educational content based on simulation results.
items.guidance: Create annual awareness calendar: Monthly tips, Quarterly phishing simulations, Annual full training. Use built-in Microsoft training content or custom materials. Tailor content by role (executives, IT, general staff).
items.verification: Awareness calendar created and followed. Training completion rates monitored. Phishing click-through rates reduced over time.

items.label: Configure communication compliance for education
items.description: Set up communication compliance policies to monitor student and staff communications for inappropriate content, bullying, harassment, and policy violations.
items.guidance: Microsoft Purview > Communication Compliance > Create policy: Monitor incoming/outgoing email and Teams messages for: harassment, threats, hate speech, inappropriate content. Assign reviewers (designated safeguarding staff). Configure alert severity levels and escalation. Start with audit-only mode.
items.verification: Communication compliance policies active. Potentially harmful communications flagged for review. Safeguarding team trained on review process. False positives tuned over time.

items.label: Configure insider risk for education data
items.description: Set up insider risk policies to detect potential data exfiltration of student records, grade manipulation, or unauthorized access to sensitive education data.
items.guidance: Microsoft Purview > Insider Risk Management > Create policies for education scenarios: Data theft by departing staff (grade export, student record download), Unauthorized access to student records outside working hours, Mass download of exam materials. Start in audit mode with priority user groups for faculty with sensitive data access.
items.verification: Insider risk policies configured for education. Alerts reviewed by designated team. False positives tuned. Student record access monitored for anomalous patterns.

items.label: Document all security policies
items.description: Create and maintain comprehensive security policy documentation covering all baseline controls, including acceptance criteria and exception processes.
items.guidance: Create security policy document covering: Access Control, MFA, Password, Device Security, Email Security, Data Protection, Incident Response, Acceptable Use. Store in central repository. Review annually.
items.verification: Security policies documented and accessible. All engineers can locate and reference policies. Policies reviewed and updated annually.

items.label: Document exclusions and exceptions
items.description: Formally document all security exclusions and exceptions with business justification, risk acceptance, review date, and approver.
items.guidance: Create exception register: Date, Requestor, Control exemption, Justification, Risk level, Approver, Review date. Require management approval for all exceptions. Set maximum 90-day exception period.
items.verification: Exception register maintained. No unapproved exceptions. Exceptions reviewed before expiry and either closed or re-authorised.

items.label: Document escalation paths
items.description: Document incident escalation paths for engineering, management, and security incidents. Ensure all team members know when and how to escalate.
items.guidance: Document: Tier 1 (standard support) > Tier 2 (senior engineer) > Tier 3 (security specialist) > Management (client communication). Include after-hours contact details. Post in team communication channels.
items.verification: Escalation paths documented and shared. Team members can recite escalation process. Escalation paths tested quarterly via drills.

items.label: Update disaster recovery documentation
items.description: Maintain current disaster recovery and business continuity documentation for Microsoft 365. Include RPO/RTO targets and recovery procedures.
items.guidance: Document: Backup procedures (mailbox, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams), Recovery procedures (item-level, full restore), RPO/RTO targets for each workload, Testing schedule. Update quarterly.
items.verification: DR documentation current. Recovery procedures tested annually. RPO/RTO targets being met. Documentation stored in accessible location.

items.label: Schedule monthly security reviews
items.description: Schedule and conduct monthly security review meetings to discuss incidents, vulnerabilities, baseline compliance, and improvement actions.
items.guidance: Monthly agenda: Incident review (last 30 days), Vulnerability status, Baseline compliance progress, Secure Score update, New threats/risks, Action items from previous month. Invite all engineering and management.
items.verification: Monthly security review meetings held. Minutes documented. Action items tracked to closure. Review demonstrates month-over-month improvement.

items.label: Schedule quarterly access reviews
items.description: Conduct quarterly access reviews for all privileged roles, guest users, and external sharing permissions.
items.guidance: Use Entra ID Access Reviews. Create review campaigns for: Privileged roles (quarterly), Guest users (quarterly), Group memberships (semi-annually). Auto-remove stale access based on reviewer decisions.
items.verification: Access reviews completed on schedule. Stale access automatically removed. Review results documented and filed.

items.label: Review admin accounts quarterly
items.description: Review all administrative account assignments quarterly to ensure least privilege principle is maintained.
items.guidance: Export all role-assignable admin accounts. Review each assignment: Is the role still needed? Has the user's responsibilities changed? Use Entra ID Access Reviews if P2 licensed.
items.verification: Admin account review completed quarterly. Role assignments updated. Unnecessary assignments removed.

items.label: Review guest access quarterly
items.description: Review all guest user accounts and their permissions quarterly. Remove guests with expired or no longer justified access.
items.guidance: Export guest users list. Review: Is access still needed? Has the collaboration project ended? Use Entra ID Access Reviews if P2 licensed. Remove stale guests.
items.verification: Guest access reviewed quarterly. Stale guests removed. Guest access aligned with active collaboration needs.

items.label: Review licensing utilisation
items.description: Audit Microsoft 365 licensing usage to ensure correct licensing for security features. Identify under-licensed users who should be upgraded for security coverage.
items.guidance: M365 Admin Center > Billing > Licenses > License usage report. Review: Unassigned licenses, Users on lower SKUs who need P1/P2/E5 features, License cost vs security value. Recommend upgrades where needed.
items.verification: Licensing review completed quarterly. Under-licensed users identified and upgraded where justified. License utilisation optimised.
